result.title: SlowLab: Benchmarking Autonomous AI Agents on a Year of Experiments They Cannot Undo
result.comment: 16 pages (9 main text), 7 figures, 5 tables. Code: https://github.com/dingningpei/slowlab-benchmark
result.summary: AI agents are increasingly proposed as autonomous experimenters, yet the benchmarks that test them mostly offer cheap experiments that answer at once. Experiments in physical facilities are different: they take months, occupy scarce equipment and cannot be undone. We present SlowLab, a benchmark in which an agent runs a one-year campaign in four simulated greenhouse compartments on a site whose crop, facility and prices are hidden. The agent decides when to plant which climate policy, whether to stop a crop and which measurements to read while crops grow, and at the end recommends one policy, which a private evaluator scores in weather the agent never saw. In a preregistered study on 48 unseen sites, three low-cost language-model agents ended near a standard grower setting and clearly below a Bayesian-optimisation baseline that starts from that setting. They ran the facility as two synchronous batches, so measurements taken during the season never changed what they planted, and these measurements improved no method's result. Letting other methods re-read the evidence a campaign had collected did not yield significantly better recommendations, which points to where the models start and which experiments they try. Code is released under the MIT license.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SlowLab 基准：智能体在隐藏作物、设施与价格的四个模拟温室中开展为期一年的实验campaign，需决定种植时机、气候策略、是否中止作物以及读取哪些测量，最后推荐一个由私有评估器在未见天气下打分的策略，并与贝叶斯优化基线对比。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文发现季节内读取的测量从未改变后续种植决策、重读已有证据也未显著改善结果，这与 LVR 中视觉证据是否真正进入推理、信息坍缩及 LOOK/STOP 时机问题同构，可供核查其评价设计。
